questions.enonce_markdown: Citizenship which is acquired naturally from one's parents is referred to as citizenship by ...
questions.corrige_markdown:
Citizenship can be acquired in different ways. Citizenship by **descent** is acquired naturally, because a child takes the nationality of his or her parents. Naturalization is a legal procedure by which a foreigner who meets the conditions set by law is granted citizenship. Adoption is not a natural way, and loyalty is a quality of a good citizen, not a way of acquiring citizenship.

**Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Which of the following is an important political right of a Cameroonian citizen?
questions.corrige_markdown:
Political rights are the rights that allow citizens to take part in the government of their country: the right to vote, to stand for election, to join a political party and to take part in public affairs. The right to vote is therefore the political right. The right to work is an economic right; the right to settlement (to live where one chooses in the country) and the right to freedom are civil or personal rights.

**Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The marriage where one woman gets two or more men as husbands is called ...
questions.corrige_markdown:
Polyandry is the form of marriage in which one woman has two or more husbands at the same time. Polygyny is the opposite: one man with two or more wives. Polygamy is the general word for having more than one spouse (it covers both polygyny and polyandry) and monogamy is marriage between one man and one woman. The question describes one woman with several men, so the exact term is polyandry.

**Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Identify the MOST important duty of a child towards the parents.
questions.corrige_markdown:
The basic duty of every child towards his or her parents is to love them, respect them and obey them. Providing for and protecting parents are duties that fall on adult children, and excellent performance (at school) is desirable but is not the main duty. Love, respect and obedience apply to children of every age and are the basis of a good family life.

**Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: A group of families that share the same ancestors is called a ...
questions.corrige_markdown:
A clan is a group of related families who trace their descent from a common ancestor. A village is a settlement where people live (its inhabitants may belong to different clans). A tribe or an ethnic group is a larger community made of several clans sharing the same language and culture.

**Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
Identify the road sign that prohibits overtaking.

![fig-1](gce-ol-citizenship-2019-p1-officiel-cameroun_exercice_1_fig_1.png)

*Signs as they appear on the scanned page (the print is grainy):* 1) a car with a diagonal bar across it, 2) a downward arrow, 3) two vehicles (a lorry and another vehicle) with a diagonal bar, inside a square panel, 4) an upward arrow and a downward arrow separated by a diagonal bar.

*Options as printed:* A) 1.   B) 2.   C) 3.   D) 4.
questions.corrige_markdown:
A road sign that prohibits overtaking is a regulatory (prohibition) sign: it shows two vehicles side by side, one passing the other, and tells drivers not to overtake. In the printed figure, sign 3 shows two vehicles one beside the other, which is the overtaking pictogram. Sign 2 is a simple arrow (a direction sign), sign 4 shows two arrows in opposite directions (it concerns two-way traffic) and sign 1 shows a single vehicle with a bar.

**Intended answer: C (3).**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.

questions.enonce_markdown: Who owns lay private schools in Cameroon?
questions.corrige_markdown:
In Cameroon, schools are public (owned by the State), confessional private schools (owned by religious bodies such as the missions) or lay private schools. Lay private schools are non-religious schools owned by private individuals or private groups, so the owners are individuals. Missionary bodies own confessional schools, and public institutions own public schools.

**Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
How can student-student relationship be BEST promoted in a school milieu?

*Options as printed:* A) Group discussion.   B) Friendship.   C) Excursions.   D) Club activities.
questions.corrige_markdown:
Good relationships among students are built when students from different classes, ethnic groups and backgrounds work and play together regularly and with a common goal. School clubs (for example civic, debating, drama or environment clubs) bring them together in a lasting way. Group discussion, friendship and excursions also help, but they are limited to class work (group discussion), to a few people (friendship) or occasional (excursions).

**Intended answer: D (Club activities).**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.

questions.enonce_markdown:
A Social ill common to schools in Cameroon is ...

*Options as printed:* A) late coming.   B) examination fraud.   C) proliferation of sects.   D) corruption by students.
questions.corrige_markdown:
A social ill is a harmful behaviour that spoils social life. In Cameroonian schools, examination fraud (cheating, copying, buying questions or marks) is a very common social ill. Late coming is a form of indiscipline rather than a social ill, while sects (secret cults) and corruption by students are also harmful but less general.

**Intended answer: B (examination fraud).**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.

questions.enonce_markdown: In Cameroon, pastoral villages describe villages whose main activity is ...
questions.corrige_markdown:
The word pastoral comes from pastoralism, the rearing of animals such as cattle, sheep and goats. A pastoral village is therefore a village whose inhabitants live mainly from animal rearing. Fishing villages live on fishing and hunting villages on hunting. The training of Pastors (church ministers) has nothing to do with the word in this context.

**Answer: A.**
themes: rural and urban life in cameroon

questions.enonce_markdown: The movement of most young people from villages to towns and cities can be referred to as ...
questions.corrige_markdown:
Migration is the movement of people from one place to another to settle. The movement from the countryside (rural area) to towns and cities (urban area) is called **rural-urban migration** or rural exodus. Urban-rural migration is the reverse movement, and inter-city movement is a movement between towns.

**Answer: C.**
themes: rural and urban life in cameroon

questions.enonce_markdown: Councils in Cameroon are directly under the control of the ...
questions.corrige_markdown:
Councils are local authorities (decentralised local government bodies). Their supervisory authority is the ministry in charge of decentralisation and local development. Among the options, the Ministry of Decentralization is the one in charge of councils. The Ministry of Urban Development, the Ministry of Town Planning and Housing and the Ministry of Finance have other roles (urban planning, housing and public finance respectively).

**Answer: D.**

choix.texte: Ministry of Town Planning and Housing.

questions.enonce_markdown: The natural environment is important to man in all of the following EXCEPT ...
questions.corrige_markdown:
The natural environment gives man food (crops, fish, game), raw materials (timber, minerals, water) and the space and resources for human activities. Manufactured goods, however, are made by man in industries from raw materials: they are not supplied by nature directly. So the exception is the supply of manufactured goods.

**Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: How can citizens protect their environment?
questions.corrige_markdown:
Citizens protect the environment by actions that keep or restore nature, such as planting trees (reforestation), keeping their surroundings clean and avoiding bush fires. Building roads and houses can damage the environment if it is not controlled, and overgrazing destroys the vegetation and the soil.

**Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
Which Ministerial department in Cameroon is responsible for the protection of biodiversity?

*Options as printed:* A) Ministry of Forestry and Wild life.   B) Ministry of Environment and Nature Protection.   C) Ministry of Water and Mineral Resources.   D) Ministry of Economy and Finance.
questions.corrige_markdown:
Protecting biodiversity (the variety of plant and animal life) is the mission of the ministry in charge of the environment and nature protection. The ministry in charge of forests and wildlife manages forest and wildlife resources and is also involved, but the ministry named after the protection of the environment and nature is the one that coordinates environmental policy and biodiversity conservation. The ministries of water and minerals and of economy and finance are not concerned.

**Intended answer: B (Ministry of Environment and Nature Protection).**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.

questions.enonce_markdown: Who represents the Head of State at the Divisional level?
questions.corrige_markdown:
In the territorial administration of Cameroon, the Governor heads the Region, the Senior Divisional Officer (SDO) heads the Division and the Divisional Officer (DO) heads the Sub-Division. These administrative authorities represent the Head of State and the Government in their areas: at the divisional level, it is the Senior Divisional Officer. The Governor does so at regional level and the Divisional Officer at sub-divisional level. A Government Delegate is linked to urban councils and is not the representative of the Head of State at divisional level.

**Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Select the Region with the highest number of Divisions in Cameroon.
questions.corrige_markdown:
The Centre Region has ten Divisions, more than any other Region. The Far North has six, the West has eight and the Littoral has four. So the Region with the highest number of Divisions among the options is the Centre.

**Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The Chief executive of a Region is a ...
questions.corrige_markdown:
Each of the ten Regions is headed by a Governor, appointed by the President of the Republic, who is the chief executive of the Region and the representative of the Head of State there. The Senior Divisional Officer heads a Division and the Divisional Officer heads a Sub-Division.

**Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The Social and Cultural Affairs service in the Governor's office is responsible for the following EXCEPT ...
questions.corrige_markdown:
The Social and Cultural Affairs service handles matters of social life and culture at the regional level: leisure and recreation, tourism, youth and sports. Civil protection (protection of people and property in case of disaster) is a security and administrative matter handled by other services of the territorial administration, so it is the exception.

**Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Which term BEST describes the act of favouring people from the same ethnic group?
questions.corrige_markdown:
Tribalism is the attitude of loyalty to one's own tribe or ethnic group, shown in favouring people from the same group over others. Favoritism is general (favouring anybody), nepotism is favouring one's relatives (family members) and ethnicity is simply the fact of belonging to an ethnic group. So the best term is tribalism.

**Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Identify the age group linked to Juvenile Delinquency.
questions.corrige_markdown:
Juvenile delinquency means offences or anti-social behaviour committed by young people who are not yet adults. Among the options, the range of 7 to 17 years is the one that corresponds to the juvenile (minor) age, from the age of criminal responsibility up to the age before adulthood. The range 0-10 includes small children, and 21 years and above is adulthood.

**Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: In which MAJOR way is corruption manifested in Cameroon?
questions.corrige_markdown:
Corruption takes several forms. The most common and most visible form in daily life is bribery: giving or receiving money or gifts to obtain a service or a favour that one is not entitled to (for example to obtain a document or to avoid a fine). Extortion, fraud and embezzlement also exist, but bribery is the one generally given as the major way in which corruption shows itself.

**Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Wayward children in Cameroon are sent for reformation to ...
questions.corrige_markdown:
Wayward children are children with bad behaviour or in conflict with the law. They are not sent to prison with adults: they are placed in rehabilitation (reformation) centres, where they are re-educated and trained so that they can return to society.

**Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Identify one major way to fight corruption in Cameroon.
questions.corrige_markdown:
Corruption is fought by prevention and by punishment. Bringing corrupt persons to trial and imprisoning those found guilty is a major way to fight it, as it deters others. Torture and arbitrary arrest are violations of human rights and cannot be used, and the seizure of property without a court decision is not a lawful method either.

**Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: "Operation Antelope" was launched by the Cameroon Government to fetch out ...
questions.corrige_markdown:
Operation Antelope was a campaign of the Government to clean the public service payroll by identifying and removing ghost workers, that is, people paid as civil servants who do not really work or do not exist. It was one of the measures against corruption and embezzlement of public funds.

**Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
Identify the political slogan that calls on Cameroonians to close ranks and work for the political economic and social progress of Cameroon.

*Options as printed:* A) National unity.   B) Operation Green Revolution.   C) National Integration.   D) Operation Green Sahel.
questions.corrige_markdown:
A political slogan is a short phrase used by a government to mobilise citizens. National Integration is the slogan that calls on all Cameroonians to close ranks, set aside their differences and work together for the political, economic and social progress of the nation. Operation Green Revolution and Operation Green Sahel are agricultural and environmental campaigns, and national unity is a value and an objective rather than the slogan named in the question.

**Intended answer: C (National Integration).**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.

questions.enonce_markdown: What is the significance of the Green colour on the flag of Cameroon?
questions.corrige_markdown:
The Cameroon flag has three vertical stripes (green, red and yellow) with a yellow star on the red stripe. Green stands for hope and for the forests of the southern part of the country (peace, life and abundant forest in the South), red stands for unity and yellow for the sun and the savannah of the North.

**Answer: B.**

choix.texte: Peace, hope, life and abundant forest in the South.

questions.enonce_markdown: In which year was the Cameroon Federal Constitution drafted?
questions.corrige_markdown:
The Federal Constitution was drawn up in 1961, after the reunification talks held at Foumban, and it created the Federal Republic of Cameroon made of East Cameroon and West Cameroon. 1960 was the year of independence of French Cameroon, 1972 is the year of the Unitary Constitution (after the referendum), and 1992 is not the year of the federal text.

**Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: What Constitutional amendment on February 4th 1984 affected the Unitary Constitution of 1972?
questions.corrige_markdown:
In February 1984 an amendment changed the official name of the country from the United Republic of Cameroon to the Republic of Cameroon. The other options refer to other changes made at different times (the post of Prime Minister was brought back in the 1970s, and the changes concerning the number of Provinces and the line of succession came with other texts).

**Answer: A.**

choix.texte: The name of the Country changed from United Republic to the Republic of Cameroon.
The post of Prime Minister was reintroduced.
The number of Provinces increased from 7-10.
The Prime Minister became the Constitutional heir of the President.

questions.enonce_markdown: Members of Government make-up part of the ...
questions.corrige_markdown:
There are three arms (powers) of government: the executive, which carries out the laws (the President, the Prime Minister and the members of Government, that is the ministers); the legislature, which makes laws (Parliament); and the judiciary, which interprets the law and settles disputes (the courts). Members of Government belong to the executive arm.

**Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The correct number of members in the National Assembly and Senate respectively is ...
questions.corrige_markdown:
The National Assembly has 180 members (deputies) and the Senate, set up in 2013, has 100 members (senators). The order in the question is Assembly first, then Senate, so the correct pair is 180 and 100.

**Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: In which way is the Legislature related to the Judicial arm of Government in Cameroon?
questions.corrige_markdown:
The relation between the two arms is that the legislature (Parliament) makes laws and the judiciary (the courts) interprets and applies them in the cases brought before it. Executing laws is the work of the executive, not of the judiciary, and the judiciary is neither created nor appointed by the legislature.

**Answer: B.**

choix.texte: Laws enacted by parliament are interpreted by the judiciary.
The legislature makes laws and the judiciary executes them.
Members of the legislature appoint those of the judiciary.

questions.enonce_markdown:
In the process of compiling election results void ballots are ...

*Options as printed:* A) not counted.   B) destroyed.   C) shared among contestants.   D) counted and noted.
questions.corrige_markdown:
A void (invalid or spoilt) ballot is a ballot paper that is not correctly filled (for example it is marked for several candidates, carries a sign or is torn). It is not counted as a vote for any candidate. The polling officials record the number of void ballots in the minutes of the polling station, but these ballots are not shared among the contestants and are not simply destroyed.

**Intended answer: A (not counted).**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.

questions.enonce_markdown: A form of electoral malpractice in which certain categories of people are systematically deprived of the voting right is called...
questions.corrige_markdown:
Disenfranchisement is the act of taking away or denying the right to vote to a person or a group (for example by refusing to register them or by removing their names from the voters' list). Marginalization and discrimination are wider notions, and disengagement means withdrawing from something.

**Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Identify the phrase which is NOT an electoral malpractice.
questions.corrige_markdown:
Electoral malpractices are acts that break the electoral rules. Not putting the ballot paper in the envelope, putting two ballot papers in one envelope (which makes the vote void) and leaving the polling booth with unused ballot papers are irregularities. Voting in secret is the right way to vote: the secrecy of the vote is a principle of free elections, so it is not a malpractice.

**Answer: B.**

choix.texte: Ballot paper not enclosed in the envelope.
Two ballot papers in the same envelope.
Leaving the polling booth with unused ballot papers.

questions.enonce_markdown: What is the full meaning of the CFA Francs?
questions.corrige_markdown:
CFA stands for Communauté Financière Africaine (African Financial Community). In Central Africa, where Cameroon belongs, the franc is also explained as the franc of the Financial Cooperation in Central Africa. Among the options, the one that gives the French words correctly is Communauté Financiere Africaine; the other options are not the official names.

**Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: One IMPORTANT measure adopted to safeguard the security of workers in Cameroon is the ...
questions.corrige_markdown:
Workers' security means protecting workers against risks such as old age, sickness and accidents at work. In Cameroon this is done through social security: employers and workers must contribute to the National Social Insurance Fund, which pays pensions, family allowances and compensation for accidents at work. Creating jobs, housing and a common retirement age are useful but are not the main security measure.

**Answer: B.**

choix.texte: compulsory contribution to the Social Insurance Fund.

questions.enonce_markdown:
The most serious challenge to rapid economic growth in Cameroon is ...

*Options as printed:* A) tax evasion.   B) laxity in the public service.   C) poor transport infrastructure.   D) weak private sector.
questions.corrige_markdown:
Economic growth needs goods and people to move easily from production areas to markets, ports and borders. Poor transport infrastructure (bad roads, few railways, weak ports) raises costs and slows trade, and is often given as the most serious obstacle to rapid growth. Tax evasion, laxity in the public service and a weak private sector also hold growth back, which is why the key is open to discussion.

**Intended answer: C (poor transport infrastructure).**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.

questions.enonce_markdown:
An IMPORTANT factor for economic growth is ...

*Options as printed:* A) state subvention.   B) the size of the population.   C) privatization.   D) a good banking system.
questions.corrige_markdown:
A good banking system collects savings and lends them to firms and households for investment, which allows production to expand and the economy to grow. State subventions, the size of the population (a big population is not enough without skills and jobs) and privatization may help in some situations but are not the key factor in themselves.

**Intended answer: D (a good banking system).**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.

questions.enonce_markdown: Identify one IMPORTANT way by which the Government of Cameroon generate revenue.
questions.corrige_markdown:
Public revenue is the money the State receives to finance public spending. The most important regular source is the collection of taxes and duties (income tax, value added tax, customs duties and others). External trade, agriculture and privatization also contribute but are less direct and less regular than taxes.

**Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: When human rights are described as "Man's inalienable rights" it means ...
questions.corrige_markdown:
Inalienable means that cannot be taken away, given up or transferred to another person. Human rights are inalienable because every person has them naturally, simply because he or she is a human being: nobody, including the State, can take them away. The other options describe the duty of the State, or particular rights.

**Answer: A.**

choix.texte: man's natural rights that cannot be transferred.
rights that a government is supposed to promote and protect.
the right to protection and equality before the law.
the right to participate in decision making.

questions.enonce_markdown: A human right violation that involves mass killing of people on account of their ethnic origin is called ...
questions.corrige_markdown:
Genocide is the deliberate killing of a large number of people because they belong to a particular national, ethnic, racial or religious group, with the aim of destroying the group. Torture is the infliction of severe pain on a person, harassment is repeated unwanted behaviour and arbitrary arrest is detention without legal grounds.

**Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
Which instrument is used for the protection of human rights in Cameroon?

*Options as printed:* A) African Charter on human and People's Right.   B) New Criminal Procedure Code.   C) Universal Declaration of Human Right.   D) Convention on the Elimination of Torture.
questions.corrige_markdown:
Human rights in Cameroon are protected by national laws and by international instruments that Cameroon has accepted. The national instrument that protects the rights of persons arrested, detained and tried (presumption of innocence, rights of the defence, limits on custody) is the Criminal Procedure Code. The three other options are international or regional texts and are also relevant, so the question is open to discussion.

**Intended answer: B (New Criminal Procedure Code).**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.

questions.enonce_markdown: A formal agreement between hostile nations that end a state of war is called ...
questions.corrige_markdown:
A peace treaty is the formal agreement signed by countries that were at war, which officially ends the state of war and settles the conditions of peace. An armistice, a truce and a cease fire agreement only stop the fighting, often for a time, without settling the dispute.

**Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: An organ of the UNO with the principal objective of maintaining World Peace and Security is the ...
questions.corrige_markdown:
The Security Council is the organ of the United Nations that has the main responsibility for maintaining international peace and security. It can impose sanctions or authorise peacekeeping missions. The General Assembly is the forum of all member states, the International Court of Justice settles legal disputes between states and the Economic and Social Council deals with economic and social questions.

**Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
A type of conflict that cuts across national borders is referred to as ...

*Options as printed:* A) Civil war.   B) International Conflict.   C) Inter-ethnic conflict.   D) Regional conflict.
questions.corrige_markdown:
A conflict that cuts across national borders is not confined to one country: it spreads from one country to its neighbours and affects a whole region, so it is called a regional conflict. A civil war takes place inside one country, an international conflict is between states and an inter-ethnic conflict is between ethnic groups, which may or may not cross borders. The wording of the options makes the key open to discussion.

**Intended answer: D (Regional conflict).**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.

questions.enonce_markdown: A situation in the world whereby men and women are given the same treatment and opportunities is known as:
questions.corrige_markdown:
Gender equality means that women and men have the same rights, treatment and opportunities (in education, work and public life). Gender bias, stereotypes and discrimination are the opposite: unfair ideas or treatment based on sex.

**Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
Minority rights have been protected in all the following ways EXCEPT...

*Options as printed:* A) the spread of educational facilities to them.   B) allowing forest dwellers to live in their habitat.   C) promotion of their cultural activities on radio and television.   D) representation in government department and appointments.
questions.corrige_markdown:
Minority and indigenous groups (for example forest dwellers) are protected by measures such as respect for their way of life and habitat, promotion of their culture in the media, access to education and representation in public life. The question asks for the one that is NOT such a measure, but each of the four options can be presented as a measure of protection, so no single option can be given as the sure answer from the text alone. For self-assessment: explain which of the four you consider the weakest protection measure and why.

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.

questions.enonce_markdown: The use of children in hawking goods on the streets is a form of ...
questions.corrige_markdown:
Child labour means making children do work that is unsuitable for their age and that harms their health, their schooling and their development. Making children sell goods in the streets (hawking) is a typical example of child labour. Trafficking is the transport or sale of children, abuse is bad treatment and torture is the infliction of severe pain.

**Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Identify an IMPORTANT cause of refugee crisis in Africa.
questions.corrige_markdown:
A refugee is a person who flees his or her country because of persecution or danger. In Africa the main cause of refugee crises is armed conflict, in particular civil wars, which force large numbers of people to flee across borders to find safety. Poverty, natural disasters and economic stagnation cause hardship and movement of people, but not on the same scale.

**Answer: A.**
